phenomenon_scale.structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Eohippus angustidens (78 µm, detail scale)

paleobiology.predecessor_note: Eohippus angustidens is stage 1 of 1 in its own chronoseries, so there is no earlier E. angustidens stage. The phenotypic outgroup is a phenacodontid condylarth; it is not assigned a Turing wavelength in this slot.

what_changes_at_this_scale.versus_predecessor: No prior E. angustidens chronospecies. At 78 µm the new quantity is a cell-biological wavelength (about 6.5 keratinocyte diameters), which a pre-equid outgroup comparison would not change merely by naming the genus.
what_changes_at_this_scale.versus_same_age_organ_scale: The organ-tier sibling for this species uses lambda = 3.3 mm (0.003298 m, tier 6_organ_mm). Wavenumber ratio k_detail/k_organ = 0.003298/7.752e-05 = 42.54. This slot resolves the chromatophore spacing that the organ-scale model coarse-grains into a single pigment stripe. Diffusion ratio, rate constants, and domain size are refit here and are not copied from that sibling.
what_changes_at_this_scale.versus_successor_orohippus: From Wasatchian Eohippus (52.0 Ma) to Bridgerian Orohippus (representative 48 Ma) body mass and cheek-tooth relief increase (MacFadden 1986 Cope's Law scaling; Froehlich 2002 taxonomy) while the manus stays tetradactyl. The cellular Turing wavelength is predicted to stay near 78 µm because D and the kinetic Jacobian are cell-biological, not autopod-size, parameters. Organ-scale stripe count N = L_flank/lambda_c can still increase if flank length grows. Delta lambda_c(cellular) across this step is therefore the conserved quantity; Delta N_organ is not.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: du/dt = D_u lap u + a - u + u^2 v; dv/dt = D_v lap v + b - u^2 v
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = largest real eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v); lambda_c = 2 pi / k_c
equations.turing_conditions: trace(J) < 0; det(J) > 0; D_v f_u + D_u g_v > 0; (D_v f_u + D_u g_v)^2 > 4 D_u D_v det(J)
equations.boundary_conditions: Periodic square patch (np.roll Laplacian). The patch is an epidermal field of view, not a whole-animal flank.

parameters.notes: a and b are dimensionless Schnakenberg rates chosen for this slot. D_u and D_v (grid units) are solved from the critical-wavenumber formula so lambda_c equals 7.752e-05 m on a grid with lambda_px = 14. They are not copied from the 3.3 mm sibling and they are not laboratory diffusivities measured on equid epidermis.

empirical_claims: Turing 1952: a homogeneous chemical steady state can be unstable to a finite band of wavenumbers when the inhibitor diffuses sufficiently faster than the activator.

Murray 1981: mammalian coat markings can be read as a chemical pre-pattern whose intrinsic wavelength is selected by that band; the number of stripes or spots then scales with domain size over wavelength.
Kondo and Miura 2010: observed pigment wavelengths are typically several cell diameters, which is the regime targeted here (78 µm / 12 µm ≈ 6.5 cells).

MacFadden 1986 and Froehlich 2002: Eohippus (Hyracotherium) is the Wasatchian start of the equid body-size and dental series; later genera are larger. That size trend is an organ-scale fact. It is not, by itself, a measurement of epidermal reaction-diffusion wavelength.
This slot does not claim that a fossil of Eohippus angustidens preserves a 78 µm pigment stripe. The wavelength is the phenomenon scale under test.
